clue.text: Craftsman excels Olympic champion

parts.note: an Olympic champion wins gold, so the champion is called a gold here
one who excels over rivals beats them, so is their beater

explanation.surface: A skilled artisan outshines the winner of an Olympic event.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as a pun: something that excels an Olympic champion beats gold, which is just what this craftsman does to the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldbeater is an artisan who hammers the precious metal into thin leaf, so is a kind of craftsman.

clue.text: Early numbers of Punch ?

explanation.surface: A question about the first issues of the humorous magazine Punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The first counting numbers are one and two; a boxer's quick left followed by a right is a one-two, a punch combination.

clue.text: They dig their work-or abandon it

definitions.text: They dig their work-or abandon it

parts.words: They dig their work-or abandon it
parts.note: trench diggers literally dig at their job, while those who ditch something abandon it, so one word covers both workers who dig and quitters

explanation.surface: Workers who either love their job or walk out on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like slang for enjoying something, but here it is literal digging of trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Labourers who cut trenches are diggers by trade, and to ditch is also slang for abandon.

clue.text: Come in with award, say, for resourcefulness

parts.note: to come in is to enter

indicators.note: say signals that the word for award is taken as spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: an award is a prize

explanation.surface: Arriving with a trophy is credited to initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes PRIZE into its sound-alike PRISE, which joins ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise is initiative and boldness in undertaking projects, much the same as resourcefulness.

clue.text: Can you pick out say a Scotsman as a pillar of the church ?

indicators.note: say signals the word for pick out is taken by its sound, losing a letter in spelling

parts.note: to pick out one thing from another is to tell them apart
mon is the Scots form of man, so a Scotsman is a mon in crosswords

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking whether you could identify a Scot as a stalwart of the kirk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can you' is padding for the question 'can you TELL?'; 'say' makes TELL sound as TEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A telamon is a column carved as a male figure supporting a building, so literally a pillar.

clue.text: The Robots have a head start in this industrial district

indicators.note: have means the play's initials hold the next piece within them

parts.note: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Machines got going early in this factory region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Robots is the play R.U.R., whose initials hold H, the start of 'head'. The Ruhr is Germany's coal and steel region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr valley in western Germany is a heavy-industry heartland of mines and steelworks.

clue.text: Stimulating metal-worker ?

parts.note: a smith making riding spurs for horsemen, and spurs stimulate a horse onwards

explanation.surface: An exciting smith.
explanation.definitionFit: A spurrier is a craftsman who forges spurs, devices that urge a horse on.

clue.text: Heartless Camilla holds the glass for Tommaso the philosopher

indicators.note: holds means the remaining letters wrap round the next piece
heartless means the central letter of the name Camilla is lost

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman holds a drinking glass in honour of an Italian thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle I from CAMILLA, leaving CAMLLA, which 'holds' PANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommaso Campanella was a 17th-century Italian Dominican philosopher, author of The City of the Sun.

clue.text: City of the Sun was 8's idea of this

definitions.text: City of the Sun was 8's idea of this

parts.words: City of the Sun was 8's idea of this
parts.note: the philosopher at 8 down wrote The City of the Sun describing his ideal commonwealth

explanation.surface: A reference to a philosopher's imagined perfect city.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed count (7) does not match this six-letter answer; the grid entry is the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanella's City of the Sun describes an ideal society, an imagined perfect state of the More kind.

clue.text: Before all, a place for the driver (non-drinking)

indicators.note: before means this piece comes ahead of the word for all

parts.note: in golf the driver club strikes the ball from the tee
all is the total

explanation.surface: A motorist, before anything else, needs a spot to sit and must stay sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golfer's club, used from the TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains from alcohol entirely.

clue.text: Elementary cartoon. This is where we came in ?

definitions.text: This is where we came in ?

parts.note: air is one of the four classical elements
a cartoon strip is a comic

explanation.surface: A simple comic, and this is the moment we arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where we came in' is the cinema phrase for rejoining a film, but here it is where an aircraft landed.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is where an aircraft comes in to land.

clue.text: Gown. Peel right off

indicators.note: off means the letters for right are removed

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel, the British prime minister, gives his first name Robert

explanation.surface: A dress and an instruction to strip the correct layer away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like a verb but is Sir Robert Peel; taking RT out of ROBERT leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose outer garment, as is a gown.

clue.text: Wire down so maybe it gives a dim religious light

definitions.text: it gives a dim religious light

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the preceding words might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Run a cable down so that it produces a gloomy churchly glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dim religious light' is Milton's phrase from Il Penseroso, describing stained glass. 'maybe' rearranges WIRE DOWN SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular stained-glass window in a cathedral filters daylight into a dim coloured glow.

clue.text: Relative share allotted to the expert ?

definitions.text: Relative share allotted to the expert ?

parts.words: Relative share allotted to the expert ?
parts.note: a relative share is a ratio, but split it and you get a portion given to a pro, an expert

explanation.surface: A professional receives a comparative cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion is a part considered in relation to the whole, a relative share.

clue.text: Like one bowling along into the lead ?

definitions.text: Like one bowling along into the lead ?

parts.words: Like one bowling along into the lead ?
parts.note: a vehicle bowling along passes others to move ahead, and a cricket bowler takes an over

explanation.surface: Someone speeding along the road to get in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowling' also suggests cricket, where a bowler is taking an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing another vehicle to go ahead is what a driver does when moving into the lead.

clue.text: When it's dry outside is the motorway in for such a shock ?

indicators.note: outside means the letters for dry go round the next pieces

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
the M1 is Britain's first main motorway, London to Leeds

explanation.surface: A question whether the road suffers a jolt during a dry spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a shock' is an adjective's definition: an earthquake shock. SEC is split round IS and MI (the M1 motorway, read as letters).
explanation.definitionFit: An earthquake tremor is described as a seismic shock.

clue.text: Announce a familiar friend

explanation.surface: Declare a close companion.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hint or make known; as a noun it is a close personal confidant.

clue.text: American soldier could have been a free lad

indicators.note: could have been suggests the letters of the following words might once have formed something else

explanation.surface: A US serviceman might once have been a carefree boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have been' rearranges FREE LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American Civil War a Northern Union soldier was called a Federal.

clue.text: This clue refers to holes of course

definitions.text: This clue refers to holes of course

parts.words: This clue refers to holes of course
parts.note: the clue's own number matches the count of holes on a standard golf course

explanation.surface: A remark that the clue concerns gaps, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means 'on a golf course'; the clue is numbered with that same count.
explanation.definitionFit: A full round of golf is played over a standard course of that many holes.

clue.text: Half of us work fast without getting rich

indicators.note: without means outside, so these letters go round the other piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Half of us labour and go hungry while failing to get wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: OP and LENT go round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means wealthy and lavish.

clue.text: A boilermaker's vessel? Never!

parts.note: the proverb says a pan under observation never comes to the boil, so it never makes anything boil

explanation.surface: A denial that a pan is the work of a boilermaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'a watched pot never boils'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, a pan that is stared at never boils, so it would never be a boilermaker.

clue.text: Nymph goes without tea at the féte

indicators.note: goes without means the following letters are dropped

parts.note: Galatea is a sea-nymph of Greek myth
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nymph skips the tea at the village fair.
explanation.walkthrough: A fête is an outdoor fundraising fair, common in British villages.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public celebration, like a fête.

clue.text: Cleans odd weapons

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the word cleans are set out strangely

explanation.surface: Someone polishes unusual arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Lances are long spears carried by mounted knights.

clue.text: The fool Yorick, so unfeeling at last

definitions.text: The fool Yorick, so unfeeling at last

parts.words: The fool Yorick, so unfeeling at last
parts.note: Yorick, the jester in Hamlet, is now just a skull, so finally numb, which describes a dimwit

explanation.surface: The jester Yorick is beyond feeling at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorick was the king's jester whose skull Hamlet holds; a skull that is numb names a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A numskull is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Not all peaceful-naturally it helps to forearm us

indicators.note: not all signals that only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: Not every pacifist naturally helps us get armed in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forearm' looks like 'arm in advance' but means the arm between elbow and wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: A cardinal distinction

definitions.meaning: a Roman Catholic cardinal is addressed by that title

explanation.surface: A churchman's special honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinals are styled 'Your Eminence', and the word also means prominence or high standing.

clue.text: Get and hold good

definitions.meaning: to prevail or be established, as a custom does

explanation.surface: Acquire and keep something valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: It means acquire, and in formal use it also means to be prevalent or in force, as a rule does.

clue.text: A struggle with this opponent leads to stagnation

indicators.note: leads to says the opponent's letters rearranged produce the word stagnation

explanation.surface: Fighting this rival only results in deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly, the answer is rearranged to give STAGNATION; 'leads to' marks the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an adversary or rival.
